panels.title: contract opens and closes — all writing services
contracts opened and closed / s
panels.description: Opens count first committed inserts across legacy, Redis and no-escrow backends; reuse and rollback do not count. Closes count first committed terminal transitions, including quarantine and deletion without a prior outcome, before later Redis debit/projection work completes. Disputes and final reports remain pending until terminal closure. Observed across all scraped writing services in the selected env; Connect block/host filters do not apply. Missing counters are No data, not zero. Rates may undercount during mixed deployment, missed scrapes, process failure or unsampled CLI writes.

panels.title: open backlog growth / s — red when opens exceed closes
panels.description: Signed opened minus closed rate; the red area shows positive opening excess directly. Short positive windows can reflect arrivals and normal contract lifetime. Sustained positive growth together with a growing overdue backlog indicates insufficient closing progress. This is observed net growth, not an absolute or overdue backlog census. Observed across all scraped writing services in the selected env; Connect block/host filters do not apply. Missing counters are No data, not zero. Rates may undercount during mixed deployment, missed scrapes, process failure or unsampled CLI writes.

panels.title: observed open backlog change over selected range
panels.description: Counter-reset-aware opened increase minus closed increase over the selected dashboard range. Positive means more opens than closes; negative means more closes. This is the observed change, not an absolute or overdue backlog count. Observed across all scraped writing services in the selected env; Connect block/host filters do not apply. Missing counters are No data, not zero. Rates may undercount during mixed deployment, missed scrapes, process failure or unsampled CLI writes.

panels.title: processes exposing contract counters by service
panels.description: Current scraped series for each counter, including legitimate zero-valued counters. Compare with deployed writers to spot missing instrumentation; a nonzero count is not proof of complete fleet coverage. Graphs above remain useful observed rates without a whole-fleet attestation gate. Observed across all scraped writing services in the selected env; Connect block/host filters do not apply. Missing counters are No data, not zero. Rates may undercount during mixed deployment, missed scrapes, process failure or unsampled CLI writes.

panels.title: client transport connections
panels.description: Open client transports, aggregated per deploy block and host. This is not a distinct-device count: one resident device may own multiple transports. Distinct devices are charted on the signals and public network-stats boards.

panels.title: dropped messages / s
panels.description: Lossless drop counters by bounded drop point: destination-forward queue full, receiving resident queue full, resident abuse validation, or zero-wait receive queue admission (by boundary; the byte-rate query is hidden by default and can be toggled on for sizing). Rates are summed per host across the selected deploy blocks.

panels.title: active exchange connections
panels.description: Post-handshake exchange socket endpoints. Outbound is the logical fleet connection count; inbound is the peer-side copy of those same sockets, so do not add the two values. A host-only selection can legitimately be asymmetric.

panels.title: current exchange data TX
panels.description: Current completed exchange data-frame write rate. Grafana automatically scales bits/s to Kbps, Mbps, or Gbps. The count includes the exchange protocol's 4-byte frame header but excludes pings and handshakes.

panels.title: current exchange data RX
panels.description: Current completed exchange data-frame read rate. Grafana automatically scales bits/s to Kbps, Mbps, or Gbps. The count includes the exchange protocol's 4-byte frame header but excludes pings and handshakes.

panels.title: current exchange data frames / s
panels.description: Completed application-protocol data frames per second in each I/O direction. These are exchange packets, not kernel TCP segments; TCP segmentation and retransmission are below this measurement boundary.

panels.title: exchange data throughput
panels.description: Live exchange data-frame throughput by process-local I/O direction. Fleet TX and RX are two observations of the same inter-server traffic and should converge; never sum them into a traffic total.

panels.title: exchange protocol frames / s
panels.description: Completed exchange frames by direction and kind. Data is relayed traffic, ping is keepalive/control traffic, and handshake is connection setup. A frame is counted only after the complete frame succeeds.

panels.title: average exchange data-frame payload
panels.description: Mean data payload bytes per completed exchange frame. The query removes the fixed 4-byte exchange header from the byte/frame ratio; compare sent and received to spot partial fleet selection or rollout skew.

panels.title: active exchange connections by operation
panels.description: Post-handshake exchange endpoint history by socket direction and purpose. Outbound is the non-duplicated logical fleet count; inbound is retained as a symmetry and host-placement signal.

panels.title: H3 listener health
panels.description: Listener availability plus supervised restart and failure rates by transport, port, and lifecycle stage.

panels.title: Proxy Protocol UDP drops
panels.description: Packets rejected at the Proxy Protocol socket before QUIC, grouped by bounded reason.

panels.title: H3 carrier events / s
panels.description: Bounded datagram, stream fallback, reassembly, and queue outcomes after capability negotiation. Missing telemetry remains no-data.

panels.title: H3 carrier bytes / s
panels.description: Datagram directions include envelope bytes; stream directions count application-message bytes. Keep these carrier measurements separate.

panels.title: H3 hybrid stream queue messages
panels.description: Current occupancy and lifetime peak per process. Peaks from different processes need not have occurred together.

panels.title: H3 hybrid stream queue bytes
panels.description: Current retained backing bytes and lifetime peak per process. This measures the bounded handoff queue, not total process memory.

panels.title: H3 hybrid stream queue mean wait
panels.description: Mean recorded wait duration over the selected rate interval. An interval without waits remains no-data.

panels.title: transport delay header accepted
panels.description: Whether each connect process accepts the per-message delay header on new connections that offer it: EnableTransportDelay as the Redis move control last narrowed it (connect/transport_delay_control.go), 1 on, 0 off. The minimum per host shows a host with any process turned off.

panels.title: resident workers and process goroutines
panels.description: Live instantaneous counts per process: control and lazy forward-ingress callback workers, destination-forward workers, and idle-timeout watchers. These are owned goroutines, not completed work or distinct devices. Compare their contribution with all process goroutines; missing series remain no-data.

panels.title: lazy resident forward-ingress capability
panels.description: Executable capability per process: 1 means forward-ingress queues and workers start on first destination use. This is not traffic or readiness, and one reporting process does not prove fleet-wide rollout. An absent capability remains no-data, not disabled or healthy.

panels.title: transport admission, credential refusals and provider intent
H1 handshake results / s
panels.description: One result per H1 admission. upgraded means the carrier opened; authenticated means authorization also succeeded.

panels.title: authenticated H1 sessions
panels.description: Authenticated H1 transports whose handler has not finished cleanup, and closes by the first observed terminal event. A close reason is an observation, not a causal verdict.

panels.title: mean authenticated H1 session duration
panels.description: From successful authorization and upgrade through handler cleanup, for completed authenticated transports only, from the histogram sum and count.

panels.title: credential refusals / s
panels.description: Transport admissions refused for the credential itself, not for a failed check, by carrier, and the ten app releases refused most.

panels.title: held WebSocket credential refusals
panels.description: Refusals held open before their authorization close: currently held, offers to the hold by outcome, and releases by cause.

panels.title: client limit kicks / s
panels.description: Client limit closes sent (enforced) or computed but not sent while enforce_concurrent_clients is false (shadow).

panels.title: transports by declared provide intent
panels.description: Live transports by declared provide intent, and intent check store errors per second. A failed check fails open and retries at its next observation.

panels.title: public provider connections by app release (top 15)
panels.description: Connections from clients that provide publicly, by app release: year.month.day for recent releases, year.month for older ones, unknown when none was sent.

panels.title: contract allowance outcomes / s
panels.description: Admitted Redis or source check outcomes and refused unchecked offers. The temporary source fallback is bounded separately.

panels.title: destination resident lookups
panels.description: Lookup attempts per second (initial and reconnect are distinct; queue is the pending data at admission) and mean wall residence including failed or canceled calls. Neither is CPU time or provider evidence.

panels.title: control frames, contract creation and companion origins — all ingresses
control frames / s by ingress, message and outcome
panels.description: Frame handler completions from the HTTP route and in-band control, across every writing service. handler_ok may include a protocol-level contract rejection; it is not an ACK.

panels.title: control frame mean residence and frames in flight
panels.description: Mean handler residence including failures, from the summary sum and count, and handlers in progress, separate from HTTP requests still reading or authenticating.

targets.expr: sum by (service, ingress, message) (rate(urnetwork_connect_control_frame_seconds_sum{env="$env",instance!=""}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (service, ingress, message) (rate(urnetwork_connect_control_frame_seconds_count{env="$env",instance!=""}[$__rate_interval])), 1e-9)

panels.title: contract rejections and refusal replays / s
panels.description: Generated create-contract protocol rejections by cause and requested companion mode (not delivery or provider outcomes); route refusal cache results (hit answers without a database read); and control requests answered from the client's own recorded refusals.

panels.title: CreateContract completions / s by ingress and disposition
panels.description: Returned CreateContract calls. contract_reply does not prove delivery or provider contact.

panels.title: CreateContract stage occupancy
panels.description: Exclusive stage wall residence per second of returned calls (the mean number of calls in each stage, including cancellation and panic) beside the calls currently in each stage. The capability series counts processes that expose stage timing.

panels.title: companion origin reads and callback outcomes / s
panels.description: Origin Query-through-row-drain attempts by phase, and completed origin callbacks by selection result before the transaction commits. origin_ready does not prove a committed creation.

panels.title: companion origin lookups and waits / s
panels.description: Authoritative origin lookups by wake source (each may run primary and chained-origin reads), waits woken by an event, fallback, deadline or cancellation, and the mean lookups per completed companion request.

panels.title: contract-origin notifications / s
panels.description: Advisory notification operations by event class. A drop requires the authoritative timed recheck.

panels.title: contract reservations, net escrow snapshots and the degradation valve — all writing services
Redis contract reservations / s
panels.description: Reservation operations by outcome, including token replays; not committed contract throughput. Creation reserves with reserve-pending and reserve-pending-full before its transaction begins, and a request that published nothing releases with release-pending; reserve-owned and reserve-owned-full come only from releases that reserve inside the transaction and go flat once those are retired. After a request's first refusal, selection probes the remaining grants read-only (reserve-probe: empty, available, undecided, error) and counts each reservation a probe proves refused as skipped instead of sending it. A payer its process recently refused as exhausted first probes every grant at once (exhaustion-proof: proven when that refuses the request without any reservation or compensation, unproven when the census runs instead). The second query counts creation transactions that refused to publish a pending reservation, by reason (window_expired, released).

panels.title: Redis grant selection: mean share of the request limit
panels.description: Mean fraction of the request-owned grant selection capacity consumed, including held requests, from the histogram sum and count.

targets.expr: sum by (service, resource) (rate(urnetwork_redis_contract_selection_fraction_sum{env="$env",instance!=""}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (service, resource) (rate(urnetwork_redis_contract_selection_fraction_count{env="$env",instance!=""}[$__rate_interval])), 1e-9)

panels.title: Redis grant selection limit
panels.description: The declared per-request selection limit. Immutable process configuration, not a remaining financial balance.

panels.title: net escrow balance snapshots / s
panels.description: Mirror balance snapshots by result: creation publications, attempted admissions, attempted settlements, and settlement, quarantine, retention and scheduled refreshes. Attempts are not committed contracts or settlements.

panels.title: contract degradation valve state
panels.description: 1 while the last published state opens the valve (payers with an exhausted balance get zero cost contracts), and the opens and terminal closes in the window of the last published check.

panels.title: degradation checks, cost reads and zero-escrow contracts / s
panels.description: Valve checks by outcome, creation cache refreshes of the valve state (only zero_cost lets an exhausted payer's contract be free), and free contracts created without escrow while the valve was open.

panels.title: contract-hole projection and prober grant selection / s
panels.description: Redis contract-hole projection operations by outcome, and internal-prober positive-byte allocations by candidate selection outcome (not completed probes).

panels.title: provider intent qualification / s
panels.description: Qualification events by class, and normal client slot decisions for intent clients that failed qualification, enforced or computed in shadow mode.

panels.title: covered receiver checkpoints and client data usage / s
panels.description: Receiver checkpoints completed as finals because they covered the sender's final acknowledged bytes (counted after the settlement commit), billable byte records added to the per-client usage meter, and drained usage hashes.

panels.title: connection reconcile: unheld rows and retirements
panels.description: Each connect handler compares the rows the database holds connected under it with the connections its process holds. Unheld counts the rows the last pass found connected but not held: a final disconnect that failed, or a registration that raised after its commit. The reconcile retires such a row on its second sighting, once every registration in flight at the first has ended. Retired counts those disconnects; passes counts passes by result, and an error pass is retried after the backlog interval. Unretired counts stale rows a pass left: a retire that raised (tried after the other rows next pass) or a busy fence or row (deferred to the next pass).

panels.title: connection sync reads retried / s
panels.description: Sync rounds of live connection announcements whose read (provide changes and modes) failed. The round is skipped and retried after the sync interval, doubling with each further consecutive failure up to its bound; the transport and its row stay, and the next successful round records the skipped round's stats. Before this, each such failure tore down the client's transport, so a database outage disconnected the providers whose sync fell in it.

panels.title: connection worker writes retried / s
panels.description: Writes of live connection announcement workers that failed: the measurement publisher's latency and speed write to PostgreSQL, and the verify egress lease write to Redis. The write is retried after the sync interval, doubling with each further consecutive failure up to its bound (a lease write never later than the regular refresh), and the publisher, the lease refresh and the transport keep going; a measurement retry writes the latest cumulative snapshot. Before this, a failed measurement write ended the publisher for the rest of the connection, a failed lease refresh ended the refresh, and a failed first lease write tore down the transport.

panels.title: provider liveness lease writes / s
panels.description: Provider liveness lease writes to Redis, by host and outcome, per client. The process's one writer writes each shard once per 30 s (plus up to 3 s of jitter), one bounded 2 s script for all of the shard's clients, and new connections at once, so the lease path holds one connection of the deadline-bound pool at a time and never starves admission or debit. refreshed and refresh_failed: clients that provide for discovery (Public or Network); extended: a connection pending its first sync read whose client's lease the shard held, kept for a reconnecting provider whatever its reads do; released and release_failed: once when a read finds the client no longer providing, again only on a later read; a connection that ends writes nothing. stamped, stamp_failed and stamp_withheld: each process's handler stamp in the writer set every 5 s, withheld while any pending or providing connection has gone 75 s without a successful write; the API enforces leases only while every live handler's stamp is current, so a steady stamp_withheld on a host means the API fails open.

panels.title: handler expiry verdicts and handler retirements / min
panels.description: Handler expiry (model.CloseExpiredNetworkClientHandlers, a once-a-minute task on a taskworker) judges each connect handler whose heartbeat is older than the expiry cutoff: expired, deleted with its connection rows retired; deferred_stamped, kept because its process still stamps the provider liveness writer set; deferred_fleet, kept because the set could not vouch and fewer handlers heartbeat than went stale. Retirement is what a connect or alt process did on finding its own handler gone: detected, a heartbeat found the row gone; unanswered, a confirmation read the database did not answer, which starts the confirmation again; restored, the row was back and heartbeats resumed; shutdown, the retirement was confirmed and the process shut down so its providers register again. Expired with no detected is a handler whose process had already ended. Detected or deferred_fleet on many hosts at once is a heartbeat path failing for every process together, as on 2026-10-19. The host and block filters apply to the retirement series only.

panels.title: normalized load by host and fleet mean
panels.description: Residents per unit of capacity (cores times the inventory move_weight) of each host, as its own movers compute it every tick from the Redis load table {connect_load}, and the fleet mean the mover balances around: all residents over the capacity of the hosts not being evacuated. Fresh, non-draining records only. A host above mean x (1 + tolerance) is a balance source; a host below the mean, under the CPU guard, is a target. Every process of a host computes the same value from the same table, so max by host shows it once. No-data while the movers cannot read the table, not zero. Host imbalance is max over min across hosts (SIGNALS.md section 24.1).

panels.title: host excess above the band
panels.description: Residents each host holds above the band's upper edge, mean x (1 + tolerance) x capacity: what its balance moves shed. 0 within the band; all its residents while it is evacuated. Each process of the host sheds a share in proportion to its residents, at most MoveMaxPerTick a tick and within the Redis budget, so the excess falls over minutes, not at once. No-data while the movers cannot read the table.

panels.title: providers and residents by host
panels.description: Public provider connections and distinct residents per host, summed over its processes. Residents are the mover's unit (MOVE.md D3): once the mover is on, a host's share of them follows its share of capacity, not its DNS weight. Draining processes count here but not in the mover's load. Compare with the normalized load to tell a capacity difference from an imbalance.

panels.title: host CPU busy, as the mover sees it
panels.description: The host CPU busy fraction each process measures from /proc/stat over its 15 s publish interval and writes into its load record: the CPU the mover's guards read. No host at or above MoveTargetMaxCpu (0.75) is a target, and a host at or above MoveEmergencyCpu (0.95) for MoveEmergencyTicks (3) ticks sheds idle clients with compulsory moves. max by host over its processes. No-data while a process cannot measure it, for example its first interval.

panels.title: moves out and in / min by host
panels.description: Moves out: the moves each source host's movers sent. Sent to: the same sends by the host they named. Arrived: handoffs by intent at the target of the mover's kinds, advisory and compulsory (urnetwork_connect_moves_arrived_total, counted by the move primitives at the target process); same-host drain arrivals are left out. The host and block filters select the counting process: the source for sends, the target for arrivals. Sent minus arrived is declines, failures and intents that expired; the success ratio is SIGNALS.md section 24.2. Counter rates per process, summed.

panels.title: moves sent / min by kind and trigger
panels.description: Moves the movers sent, by kind (advisory or compulsory) and trigger: balance, a host above the band; arrival, a client that just arrived on a source host (EnableArrivalMoves, off by default); evacuation, a host listed in the control's evacuateHosts; emergency, a host whose CPU stayed at or above MoveEmergencyCpu. Drain moves are the drain's, not the mover's, and do not appear here. The fleet budget is MoveMaxPerMinute, at most what the control's maxPerMinute allows.

panels.title: mover mode
panels.description: Each process's effective mode after the Redis control {connect_move}control narrowed the code settings: 0 off, 1 dry run, 2 on. Off is the code default (MoveDefaultMode), so a deploy moves nothing until an operator sets the control; EnableMove off holds every process at 0 whatever the control says. A process that cannot read the control reports 0 for that tick. Mixed values across processes mean failing control reads or processes of another build.

panels.title: dry-run would-send and budget refusals / min
panels.description: Would send: the moves a dry-run mover chose and the budget reserved, by source and target, which it did not send (no cooldown, intent or frame). Compare with the host excess before turning the mover on. Refused: reservations the Redis per-minute budget refused, by the cap that refused: fleet (MoveMaxPerMinute, or the control's lower maxPerMinute), source (MoveMaxPerMinutePerSourceHost) or target (MoveMaxPerMinutePerTargetHost). A steady target refusal on one host is the arrival cap protecting a new or empty host.

panels.title: move-capable residents
panels.description: Residents whose client declared resident move version 1 or later (D2), by host and as a share of all residents: the rollout adoption of the client library. Advisory moves only go to them. Counted by each mover tick, which runs in every mode; no-data on a process whose mover does not run.

panels.title: mover ticks, send errors and load publishes / min
panels.description: Mover ticks by outcome: off, draining, store_error (a Redis read or write failed and the tick failed closed), no_load (no fresh record of its own, or no fleet mean), in_band, db_paused (the Postgres pool acquire wait was above MoveDbWaitPauseThreshold), no_target, no_candidate, budget_refused, send_failed or moved. Send errors: moves the executor did not send after the budget reserved them, by kind and trigger. Load publishes: writes of each process's record into {connect_load}, published or failed; a host whose publishes fail drops out of the table and is neither a source nor a target.

panels.title: move results / min: declined and failed
panels.description: Accepted client reports (connect/MOVE.md 5.1): a client declines an advisory move by its D11 rules, or reports a replacement that failed, with the typed reason. Reports arrive wherever the client's control path runs: the connect resident, the api's /connect/control and the proxy's in-process authority, so these series are not filtered by service, block or host. A failure counts against the target address's breaker unless the move was a drain's. No-data: no reports.

panels.title: move expiries, compulsory closes and dropped reports / min
panels.description: Expired: moves whose arrival window (MoveArrivalTimeout past the migrate time) ended with the resident still at the source; the client keeps forwarding. Compulsory closed: clients closed with the moved close (4006) at a compulsory move's deadline because their resident was still here. Dropped: reports the platform did not accept, by cause: no_intent (the intent expired or an arrival consumed it first), foreign_move or invalid_move_id (a move the client was not sent), invalid_result; these are counted wherever the control path runs. No-data: none.

panels.title: target breakers open
panels.description: 1 while moves to an inventory address are held off (connect/MOVE.md 5.5): its failure reports over sends exceeded MoveTargetBreakerRatio with at least MoveTargetBreakerMinSends sends in MoveTargetBreakerWindow, for MoveTargetBreakerTimeout. Counted per address, so one bad interface or path does not idle the whole host. Set by the processes that ask about the address; an address no process asked about has no series.

panels.title: drain refusals and drain moves / min
panels.description: A draining process refuses new client transports (h1, quic) and inbound exchange handshakes for a resident it does not have (exchange), so a redialing client lands on a sibling at once (connect/MOVE.md 2.3). Drain moves: every resident gets a compulsory move to this host's own addresses (capable=true) or the legacy migrate (capable=false), each with a drain intent. Refusals outside a drain mean a process is stuck draining while it still takes traffic. No-data: no drain.

panels.title: platform-hosted dials placed and left to DNS / min
panels.description: Edge placement (connect/MOVE.md 13, server/edgeplacement): the hosted proxy's windows (service proxy) and the URL and capability probes (service taskworker) run on the platform, so each of their dials to the platform host asks the load model the mover reads for an edge instead of leaving the edge to DNS. Placed: dials given an edge, by edge host; hosts are drawn by their headroom to the band edge. Left to DNS: dials answered none, by reason: model, no snapshot yet or the snapshot is older than its two-minute bound; off, the {connect_move}control placement is off; host, the dial is for a host other than the platform host; no_host, no host has an address that is not held after a failed dial. These processes are not connect's, so the host and block filters do not apply.

panels.title: placed dials that failed / min by edge host
panels.description: Placed addresses whose dial failed, by the edge host the process's snapshot maps the address to (unknown: an address the snapshot does not know). The dialing client reports each failed placed address, and the process then holds it from all of its clients for two minutes (FailHold). Failures concentrated on one edge host point at that edge's interface or listener; failures spread over every host point at the dialing side.

panels.title: load model reads / min by outcome
panels.description: Each placing process reads the {connect_move}control and the {connect_load} table every ten seconds, and the services.yml edge inventory every five minutes: ok, or the read that failed (inventory_failed, control_failed, load_failed). A failed read keeps the last snapshot, which stops placing once it is two minutes old (left to DNS with reason model); a failed inventory load keeps the last inventory.

panels.title: edge hosts open to placement
panels.description: Edge hosts in each placing process's latest snapshot of the load model: a fresh load record from a connect process that is not draining, capacity in the inventory, not evacuated, and a placeable interface. The CPU ceiling (MaxCpu, 0.8) applies to each dial, not to this count. Shown as the fewest and the most across each service's processes, which differ while processes hold different snapshots; a process reports 0 before its first read. Fewer hosts than the services edges put every platform-hosted dial on the rest.

panels.title: close requests and CloseSequences sent by residents / s
panels.description: Close requests residents sent to their clients, by kind (contract, peer), and the CloseSequences frames that carried them. A request asks a receiver that has not reported for its final, at the sender's final (CLIENTCLOSE.md). Alt's embedded exchange counts under service alt. No data, not zero, until a resident sends one.

panels.title: removed-client transport closes and key events dispatched / s
panels.description: Transports closed because their client was removed through the api, by kind, and the key events behind them: client-removed events dispatched to the exchange, and close-request events dispatched to registered listeners. A removal keeps the client's resident until its idle ttl (CLIENTCLOSE.md).

panels.title: unused contracts settled at the sender's zero final / s
panels.description: Unused contracts settled on the report path because the sender's final reported zero bytes and the receiver had not reported (owner rule, 2026-10-28), counted after a successful settlement commit. Without the rule they wait for the expiry sweep. Every service that settles reports counts here.
